answer:
For Linear weights shaped (fan_out,fan_in), Kaiming-normal variance is 2/fan_in for ReLU. Xavier-normal variance is 2/(fan_in+fan_out). These scales preserve approximate signal/gradient variance under their assumptions; different nonlinearities require different gains. Initialize under no_grad with an optional local generator. Bias initialization is separate.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Under independent zero-mean inputs, a linear output's variance is approximately $fan_{in}\operatorname{Var}(W)\operatorname{Var}(x)$. ReLU discards about half the second moment under symmetric assumptions, motivating Kaiming variance $2/fan_{in}$. Xavier balances forward/backward scales. These approximations are useful initializations, not guarantees that every deep architecture preserves variance indefinitely. [3](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://pouannes.github.io/blog/initialization/) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/nn.init.html).
